sources.title: Structured interview note preserving integer grouping prompt

claims.text: The repository source requires an integer to be grouped in threes with commas; language, width, negative handling, leading zeros, fractions and locale are not source-frozen.

Under the declared Java long contract, the implementation right-aligns three-digit groups, preserves a leading minus sign and matches an independent BigInteger arithmetic oracle across exhaustive small values, long extremes and 50,000 seeded random longs.

validation.command: compile exact candidate Solution.java; compile/run independent BigInteger arithmetic Reviewer.java

boundary_tests.expected: commas only between right-aligned three-digit groups
minus sign preserved and excluded from digit grouping
correct output without abs overflow in candidate
candidate matches independent BigInteger arithmetic grouping oracle
candidate matches independent BigInteger arithmetic grouping oracle

findings: Repository source only freezes the three-digit grouping plus comma requirement; language, integer width, negative handling, leading-zero semantics, fractions and locale are not source-proven.
Candidate explicitly labels Java long, preserved minus sign and plain-decimal formatting as reference choices rather than original-question facts.

The implementation aligns grouping to the right edge of the decimal digit sequence, excludes the sign from grouping, and avoids the Long.MIN_VALUE absolute-value overflow trap by never applying Math.abs.
Independent BigInteger arithmetic oracle validates all values from -10000 through 10000, fixed group boundaries and long extremes, plus 50,000 seeded random long values with no mismatch.

O(d) time and O(d) output-space claims match the single-pass implementation and unavoidable result size; the answer avoids fabricated project experience and does not smuggle locale/currency semantics into the prompt.
